title: The Pricing Page Rework
summary: Signalboard is a self-serve analytics platform where teams connect their own data and build dashboards without an engineer. Its customers are small and mid-size business teams who try it free for 14 days and subscribe monthly if it sticks — no sales team, the trial does the selling.

Q1.text: Trial-to-paid conversion is 4%, and lost-deal notes say 'too expensive.' The CEO wants a cheaper Starter tier. Where do you start?

choices.text: Redesign the pricing page with a cheaper tier front and center
choices.reveal: The new page ships fast, but conversion doesn't move — 'too expensive' was a proxy for 'unclear value,' not a price objection.

choices.text: Interview trial users who churned and users who converted about how they actually decided
choices.reveal: Churned users rarely mention price itself; they say they 'couldn't tell if it fits our workflow' — value never became visible during the trial.
choices.because: It asks the real deciders - churned and converted trial users - how they actually decided, which is the only way to tell price from value clarity.

choices.text: Analyze which pricing-page sections trial users actually visit
choices.reveal: Most trial users never open the pricing page at all — the decision is being made inside the product, not on the page.
Prices sit mid-market — undercutting would cut revenue without touching the real drop-off.

Q2.text: Churned users say they couldn't tell if the product fits their workflow; converted users all mention the same 'aha' dashboard. What do you do?

choices.text: Rewrite the pricing page to lead with the dashboard value
choices.reveal: The copy improves, but words alone don't get users to the moment the value becomes visible.

choices.text: Ask the CEO to hold the cheaper tier and present the findings first
choices.reveal: The findings reframe the problem: a cheaper tier would attract users who never reach value, adding support load at lower revenue.

choices.text: Find what converted users did differently in their first week
choices.reveal: Converted users connected real data in the first three days and built a dashboard; churned users never got past the demo dataset.
choices.because: It finds what converted users did in their first week to reach the dashboard moment, which is the behavior worth designing for.

Q3.text: Most trial users never visit the pricing page. What does that tell you?

choices.text: Treat onboarding, not the pricing page, as the conversion surface
choices.reveal: The problem is redefined: conversion happens when value becomes visible in-product, so the work moves to the trial experience.
choices.because: It infers that trial value never becomes visible on the pricing page, so the page itself is the wrong place to start.

choices.text: Add an in-app banner linking to the pricing page
choices.reveal: Clicks on the banner rise; conversion doesn't — traffic to the page was never the constraint.

choices.text: Email trial users a direct link to the pricing page
choices.reveal: Open rates are fine, conversion flat — the page explains price but doesn't create the 'fits our workflow' moment.

Q4.text: Converted users connect real data and build a dashboard in the first three days; churned users stall on the demo dataset. What do you design?

choices.text: A cheaper Starter tier, so reaching value costs less
choices.reveal: The tier converts a few price-sensitive users, but most churned users never reached value — discounting doesn't shorten their path.

choices.text: A comparison page: the product versus the spreadsheet teams use today
choices.reveal: The comparison clarifies the pitch but still asks users to imagine the fit instead of experiencing it.

choices.text: A guided first-run that connects a real dataset and builds one meaningful dashboard in session one

reveal.text: The guided first-run lifts day-3 dashboard creation from 22% to 58% in the internal pilot.

choices.because: A guided first run that gets users to the dashboard moment solves the value-clarity problem a cheaper tier cannot reach.

Q5.text: The redesigned page with the cheaper tier shipped; conversion is unchanged. What now?

choices.text: Take the evidence back: interview churned and converted users about how they decided
choices.reveal: The interviews show churned users 'couldn't tell if it fits our workflow' — value never became visible; the tier was never the issue.
choices.because: Interviewing churned users tests whether too expensive was really a price objection or a value-clarity failure.

choices.text: Keep the new tier and re-test with different headline copy
choices.reveal: Copy variants barely move conversion — the message is fine; the trial never shows the value.

choices.text: Accept the flat result and keep the new page as is
choices.reveal: The cheaper tier stays live, attracting users who never reach value — support load rises while revenue doesn't.

Q6.text: The guided first-run is designed and the pilot shows more users reaching the dashboard moment. Before full rollout, what do you do?

choices.text: Ship to all new trials and monitor conversion
choices.reveal: Conversion improves, but without a holdout group finance can't tell onboarding gains from market seasonality.

choices.text: A/B the guided first-run against the current trial for two weeks, watching trial-to-paid

reveal.text: Conversion moves from 4% to 6.5%; with the evidence in hand, the cheaper tier is quietly retired.

choices.because: A two-week holdout against the current trial attributes the conversion lift cleanly, which is what makes the cheaper tier removable.

choices.text: Present the funnel evidence and the A/B plan to the CEO before shipping anything
choices.reveal: The CEO drops the cheaper-tier push — the decision now rests on behavioral evidence instead of lost-deal anecdotes.

criteria.label: Learning how decisions are really made
criteria.guidance: Anecdotes say price; decide only after hearing the deciders.

criteria.label: Designing the value moment
criteria.guidance: Value must be experienced in session one, not explained on a page.

criteria.label: Proving the fix worked
criteria.guidance: A holdout against the current trial attributes the gain cleanly.
